program: [ [ mul ] swap cons ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map swap [ i quote cat ] fold 0 [ add ] fold
notes: ys become closures (uncons y mul); folding them over xs with body `i quote cat` pops each x, multiplies and appends, so the accumulator rotates into the products list; then sum. Four stages, 28 ops.

program: [ over ] dip [ swap sub ] swap cons map [ 0 lt? ] filter [ over ] dip cat swap [ swap ] dip [ swap sub ] swap cons map [ 0 swap lt? ] filter cat 0 [ add ] fold
notes: Total = sum xs + sum of (lo - x) over x < lo + sum of (hi - x) over x > hi: the negative hi-deficits are catted onto xs, the positive lo-deficits after them, then one sum. Assumes lo <= hi, which the sampler guarantees (lo < hi).

program: [ swap sub quote ] dip [ swap ] dip sub cons [ 0 swap lt? ] filter 0 [ add ] fold
notes: Builds the list (lo1 - hi2, lo2 - hi1), keeps the positive entries and sums them. For valid intervals (lo <= hi, as the sampler draws them) at most one entry is positive, so the sum equals max(0, max(lo1,lo2) - min(hi1,hi2)).

program: dup uncons drop [ quote ] map [ [ add ] cat ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map swap [ i quote cat ] fold uncons drop dup [ quote ] map [ [ lt? ] cat ] map [ [ false eq? ] cat ] map swap [ filter ] fold uncons swap drop
notes: The tail becomes closures (uncons x add) folded over xs with `i quote cat`, rotating xs into its neighbour sums with x_n left at the front; drop it, then take the maximum by folding the filters (s lt? false eq?) over the sums. Nine stages, 59 ops.

program: [ [ lt? ] over cons [ cons ] dip over over [ false eq? ] cat filter [ filter ] dip cat ] fold
notes: Insertion of each x into ys: X = (x . acc), then filter(X, e < x) ++ filter(X, not e < x); 18-atom body (staged: 27), 25-op segment. Blocked: the insertion needs the accumulator twice plus x in one fold step, and a single-value state cannot be duplicated, filtered twice and re-joined in 4 atoms; block-by-interval merges need a copy of the list per x, which only a bound list (counted by its length) or exponential doubling provides.
